extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent owners and third-party requesters involved in inter partes reexamination (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners (and participants) on processing inter partes reexamination proceedings, including Office action content, panel review, Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) rules, submissions after ACP, and when to reopen prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Not Within Scope of Inter Partes Reexamination (form paragraph 26.03)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is noted that an issue not within the scope of reexamination proceedings has been raised. The issue will not be considered in a reexamination proceeding. 37 CFR 1.906(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 26.03; in the bracket identify the issues. Advise patentee it may be desirable to consider filing a reissue application if claims may be partially or wholly inoperative or invalid. Such issues (e.g., public use, on-sale, conduct, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) should not be raised independently by the examiner; if independently discovered by the examiner but not raised by patent owner or third party requester, they will not be noted by the examiner (37 CFR 1.906(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action cover sheet selection and completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTOL-2064 should be used as the Office action cover sheet (for actions responsive to a patent owner response and possibly third party comments); Form PTOL-2065 should be used as the cover sheet for an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fill in the space for the date(s) of the communication(s) to which the Office action is responsive. Insert the appropriate response period ('Two' for a regular Office action responsive to a patent owner response; 'One' for an ACP response period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for Office correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP and other merit correspondence require primary examiner signature; include conferees' initials where panel review occurred per procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding paragraphs and warnings in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Office actions should include statements cautioning the patent owner that a complete response should be made since the next action is expected to be an ACP, and warn that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert form paragraph 26.05 (Papers To Be Submitted in Response to Action) and form paragraph 26.73 (Correspondence and Inquiry) at the end of the Office action followed by form paragraph 26.73 as appropriate. Explain that amendments after an ACP must include a showing of 'good and sufficient reasons' why they are necessary and were not earlier presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: 26.05 — Papers To Be Submitted in Response to Action
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure full consideration of any amendments, affidavits or declarations, or other documents as evidence of patentability, such documents must be submitted in response to this Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions after the next Office action (intended to be an ACP) will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116(b) and (d) and will be strictly enforced. Ensure documents are filed in response to the Office action to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: 26.73 — Correspondence and Inquiry routing
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence relating to this inter partes reexamination proceeding should be directed to the Central Reexamination Unit (mail, fax, hand delivery addresses provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the specified mailing address, fax number, and hand-delivery location. Direct inquiries about communications or status to the Central Reexamination Unit telephone number provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference required before Office actions (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will be conducted at each stage of the examiner’s examination in an inter partes reexamination proceeding, other than for actions such as notices of informality or incomplete response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel reviews examiner’s preliminary decision to reject and/or allow claims prior to issuance of each Office action. Matters outside examiner jurisdiction (petitions, extensions, support staff notices) are excluded from panel review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel make-up
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel will consist of three members, one of whom will be a manager; the second member will be the examiner in charge of the proceeding; the manager will select the third member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner-conferees should be primary examiners or examiners knowledgeable in the technology or experienced in reexamination practice. Majority of conferees should not have been involved in the examination or issuance of the patent. Choose an 'original' examiner only if most knowledgeable or for specific justifiable reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel process and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner must inform manager of intent to issue an Office action; manager convenes panel; if panel confirms examiner’s preliminary decision, the action shall be issued and signed by the examiner with the two other conferees initialing as 'conferee'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference does not confirm the examiner’s treatment, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action. Both conferees initial even if dissenting. If the examiner in charge disagrees with the conference decision, the manager will generally assign the proceeding to another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/outcomes expected from panel conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Each conference will provide a forum to consider all issues of patentability as well as procedural issues having an impact on patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel review by multiple primary examiners diminishes perception of undue influence, ensures matters are appropriately addressed, provides multiple perspectives so missed issues are likely detected, and yields comprehensive discussion and findings for each issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and remedy for failure to hold panel conference
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Office action is issued without panel review, the patent owner or third party requester who wishes to object must promptly file a paper alerting the Office of this fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any challenge must be made within two weeks of receipt of the Office action or it will not be considered. Failure to hold a panel review, by itself, is not grounds for vacating Office decisions or restarting the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACP content requirements — completeness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The grounds of rejection and determinations of patentability must (in the ACP) be clearly developed so that the patent owner and third party requester may readily judge advisability of filing comments after an ACP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACP should address all issues as to the patents or printed publications. It must clearly set forth each rejection proposed by the third party requester that the examiner refuses to adopt and give reasons why the third party’s proposed rejection is not appropriate. Provide comprehensive reasons for patentability for each favorable determination; can incorporate by reference a prior complete statement but must also rebut patent owner arguments and reflect consideration of third party comments. See MPEP § 1302.14 for examples of suitable statements of reasons for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of amendatory matter under 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an amendment has been submitted in the patent owner’s response, the amendatory matter (revised or newly added matter) should be reviewed for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not review content of the patent that has not been revised for 35 U.S.C. 112 in reexamination; review under 112 applies only to the new or revised matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of rejection — how to state and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection originally initiated by the examiner, such withdrawal should be clearly stated in the ACP as a decision favorable to patentability with respect to the withdrawn rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party requester may propose the withdrawn rejection as 'rejection proposed by the third party requester' in subsequent comments. If patent owner fails to respond to ACP and a RAN is issued, the third party may appeal withdrawal as a final decision favorable to patentability (37 CFR 41.61(a)(2)). Where the examiner withdraws a ground previously proposed by a third party requester, treat the issue as a rejection proposed by the third party requester that the examiner refuses to adopt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for responses set in cover sheet (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally the patent owner is given two months to respond to an Office action responsive to a patent owner response, and 'Two' should be inserted on the PTOL-2064; for an ACP, the patent owner is generally given one month and 'One' should be inserted on PTOL-2065.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specified response periods on the cover sheet; extensions may be governed by 37 CFR where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACP issuance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An ACP shall set forth all rejections and determinations not to make a proposed rejection, and the grounds therefor. An ACP will not usually close prosecution if it includes a new ground of rejection not previously addressed by the patent owner, unless the new ground was necessitated by an amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although an ACP has attributes similar to a 'final rejection,' it is not a final action and cannot be appealed until a RAN is issued. Before an ACP, a clear issue should be developed. When all claims are found patentable in the first action, the examiner should issue an ACP. The criteria for issuing an ACP is analogous to MPEP § 706.07(a) for making a rejection final.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACP substantive checklist (items to review/reiterate)
rubrics_metrics.description: In making an ACP: (A) all outstanding grounds of rejection of record should be carefully reviewed, (B) all outstanding determinations of patentability (decisions to not make a proposed rejection) of record should be carefully reviewed, and (C) any grounds of rejection relied upon and any determinations of patentability relied upon should be reiterated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure ACP clearly develops grounds/determinations so parties can judge advisability of filing comments (37 CFR 1.951(a)/(b)). If a single previous Office action contains a complete statement, ACP may incorporate by reference but must include rebuttals of patent owner arguments and reflect third party comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: One opportunity to submit comments after ACP (37 CFR 1.951(a)/(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: After an ACP the patent owner may once file written comments limited to the issues raised in the reexamination proceeding and/or present a proposed amendment to the claims; when patent owner files such comments, the third party requester may once file comments responsive to the patent owner’s submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any second or supplemental submission after ACP by either party will be returned. Submissions must be filed within the time set for response in the ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits and extensions for patent owner submission after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner submission under 37 CFR 1.951(a) must be filed within the time period set for response to the ACP (normally 30 days or one month, whichever is longer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension may be requested under 37 CFR 1.956 but the time period may not be extended to run past six months from the date of the ACP. Examiner and parties should identify and develop all issues prior to ACP, including evidence under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on content of patent owner and third party submissions after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 37 CFR 1.951(a) and (b) must be limited to the issues raised in the ACP (and for third parties, responsive to the patent owner’s comments when applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submissions address issues not raised in the ACP (or go beyond responding), they will be returned as improper and, if scanned into the Image File Wrapper, expunged from the record with notification. No additional opportunity to correct unless a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 is granted; any replacement comments permitted by petition must be strictly limited to the content of the original submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if patent owner does not file submission after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner does not timely file comments and/or a proposed amendment pursuant to 37 CFR 1.951(a), then the third party requester is precluded from filing comments under 37 CFR 1.951(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) will be issued where the time for filing patent owner comments and/or amendment has expired and no such paper has been received. Note that where patent owner chooses not to file submission under 1.951(a), no rights of appeal are lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to petition that ACP is premature (37 CFR 1.181)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner believes the ACP is premature, the patent owner may, in addition to comments under 37 CFR 1.951(a), file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 within the time period for filing the comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The third party requester may then once file comments responsive to the patent owner’s petition under 1.181 within 30 days from service of the petition on the third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner timing to take up case for action after ACP
rubrics_metrics.description: If no patent owner submission under 37 CFR 1.951(a) is received after two months from the ACP, the examiner will take up the case for action; if an extension was obtained under 1.956, wait until the extended time plus one month expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If patent owner submission is received, third party has 30 days from service to file 1.951(b) submission; if no third party submission after two months from service, examiner takes up case for action. Where both submissions have been received, take up the case as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options as to which action to issue (RAN vs reopening prosecution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) should be issued where no 1.951(a) submission has been filed by the patent owner, or where submissions have been filed and the examiner will not modify his/her position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission included a proposed amendment, RAN will indicate whether it was entered. If a submission is incomplete or defective, notify parties in RAN that it has not been considered and no additional opportunity is available since comments may only be filed 'once.' See MPEP § 2673.01 for discussion of when to issue an action reopening prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner treatment of proposed amendments after ACP (entry standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of proposed amendments submitted after the ACP will be governed by the strict standards of 37 CFR 1.116; the patent owner no longer has right to unrestricted further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments that merely cancel claims, adopt examiner’s suggestions, remove issues for appeal, or require only cursory review may be entered more easily. If entry would withdraw rejections or indicate additional claim patentable, the amendment generally raises new issues and need not be entered. Examiner encouraged to enter amendments that only add an additional claim unless entry would cause an 'undue burden' — if not entered, explain the undue burden. When multiple amendments are submitted after ACP, all except the first are returned. An amendment filed after ACP and prior to RAN may be entered where appropriate; an amendment filed after RAN will not be entered absent a grantable petition under 1.183; examiner may reopen prosecution to enter amendment and issue new ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to explain when proposed amendment not entered
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a proposed amendment is not entered, the examiner will provide a detailed explanation of the reasons for not entering the proposed amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims as amended would present a new issue requiring further consideration or search, identify the new issue and explain why a new search and/or more than nominal consideration is necessary. Parties will be notified in the RAN or Office action whether the proposed amendment will be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reopening of prosecution when examiner modifies position
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a submission after ACP has been filed and the examiner decides to modify his/her position, the examiner should ordinarily reopen prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must be given an opportunity to adequately address any change in position adverse to patent owner. A RAN cannot be issued until patent owner has had opportunity to address each and every rejection prior to appeal. Reopen prosecution where any new ground of rejection is made or any additional claim is rejected. Prosecution is ordinarily reopened by issuing a non-ACP Office action prior to the ACP stage; reopening at the ACP stage can deprive patent owner of amendment rights limited after ACP.
